title: Repeated word generation by a counter loop
statement: Let $\mathrm{pat}$ and $\mathrm{ws}$ be finite Boolean words, let $s\in\mathbb{N}$, and suppose the binary value of $\mathrm{ws}$, read least significant bit first, is $s$. Let $d$ be a configuration of a three-work-tape machine on a fixed Boolean input. Assume its state is the initial sweep phase; tape $0$, at every offset $p$ from its head with $-1\le p\le |\mathrm{ws}|$, agrees with the buffer containing $\mathrm{ws}$ from cell $0$ onward; and tape $2$ is blank at all those offsets. Put $t=4|\mathrm{ws}|+s(|\mathrm{pat}|+1)+H(\mathrm{ws},s+1)+6$, where $H(\mathrm{ws},r)=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}(2a_j+2)$ and $a_j$ is the number of initial false entries in the word obtained from $\mathrm{ws}$ by applying $j$ times the operation that subtracts one from its fixed-width binary value, with underflow wrapping to the all-true word. After $t$ steps of the repeat machine for $\mathrm{pat}$, its state is the final phase and tape $1$ contains $s$ consecutive copies of $\mathrm{pat}$ on the cells from its initial head position up to, but not including, the cell $s|\mathrm{pat}|$ positions to its right; its head has advanced by exactly $s|\mathrm{pat}|$. Every other cell and every other component of the configuration is unchanged. The final phase is not reached at any earlier time, and at every time $u\le t$, the displacement of each work-tape head from its initial position is at most $s|\mathrm{pat}|+|\mathrm{ws}|+1$.
